ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Charles Darwin Synthetic CCD

text.paragraph: Evaluation of recurrent vomiting episodes: history, symptom diary, Rome IV criteria, red flags, cannabis and substance history, anxiety and mood screens, laboratory tests, ECG, and orders for small-bowel imaging and upper endoscopy. Concerns: For more than a year he has had episodes of nausea and repeated vomiting every one to three weeks, each lasting about 12 to 36 hours, that stop his work; this winter they came almost every week; Each episode begins with nausea, sweating, trembling hands, a racing heart, and a swimming head; between episodes he has troublesome wind and tires easily, but does not vomit; He worries about being taken ill in company and has begun to avoid gatherings and travel. [S]

tr.td: Evaluation of recurrent vomiting episodes: history, symptom diary, Rome IV criteria, red flags, cannabis and substance history, anxiety and mood screens, laboratory tests, ECG, and orders for small-bowel imaging and upper endoscopy
Six-week follow-up: results, gastroenterology consultation, provisional diagnosis, prophylaxis, and abortive plan
Three-month review: amitriptyline at target dose, ECG, episode diary, and anxiety screen
Six-month review of response to prophylaxis
Same-day sick visit for a head cold

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: Work-up between episodes: blood count, metabolic and liver panels, lipase, urinalysis, TSH, morning cortisol, celiac serology, a baseline ECG, CT enterography, and upper endoscopy
Gastroenterology consultation to confirm the diagnosis and advise on prophylaxis, abortive treatment, and an emergency plan
Symptom diary: date, prodrome, length and severity of each episode, triggers, medicines taken, and emergency visits

Amitriptyline prophylaxis at bedtime: 25 mg, raised by 25 mg every two weeks to 75 mg (about 1 mg/kg), with an ECG at baseline, at about 50 mg, and at the target dose; judge the response after three months at target and continue for at least a year if it helps

Abortive plan at the first sign of the prodrome: sumatriptan 20 mg nasal spray with ondansetron 8 mg dissolving tablet, a dark quiet room, and small sips of fluid; an individualized emergency department letter for episodes that do not settle
Trigger management: regular meals and sleep, planning around travel and social events, early treatment of infections, and continued avoidance of cannabis
Anxiety and mood: GAD-7 and PHQ-9 at the first visit and every three months; relaxation breathing, with cognitive behavioral therapy offered if symptoms persist
Complete the work-up between episodes (blood and urine tests, ECG, CT enterography, and upper endoscopy) before the six-week visit
All tests normal; Rome IV criteria met; provisional diagnosis of cyclic vomiting syndrome at the consultation
At least half as many episodes after three months at the target dose of prophylaxis
About two episodes a month before treatment; one brief episode, aborted at the prodrome, in the three months before the six-month review
Carry the abortive medicines and the emergency department letter, and use them at the prodrome
The one episode since starting treatment was treated at the prodrome and settled in about ten hours without an emergency visit; letter carried
QTc below 450 ms at the target amitriptyline dose
Practice relaxation breathing most days and lower the GAD-7 score by the six-month review
Daily breathing practice; GAD-7 from 8 to 5

list.item: Episodes stop all work for one to two days, every one to three weeks; between them he works most mornings but tires by afternoon [S]
Alert, courteous, and precise; keeps careful notes of his symptoms; anxious when describing episodes in company; GAD-7 8 and PHQ-9 6, with no thoughts of death or self-harm [S]
